findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, inverted logic also present
findings.body: The function enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (i.e. enabled is true when the flag is NOT enabled), then returns false either way (both branches return false). This makes the function always return false regardless of feature flag state, meaning SQL expressions are unconditionally disabled even when intentionally wanted, and the logic is nonsensical/dead code. While this currently achieves the goal of disabling the vulnerable feature, the naming and logic are backwards and misleading, and if flag intent is ever restored this will silently remain broken. Should be a simple hard return false with a clear comment, or fixed boolean logic tied to the feature flag.

findings.title: TablesList calls RunCommands which always errors, breaking valid SQL expression configs
findings.body: db.go's RunCommands (and QueryFramesInto) stub always returns errors.New("not implemented"). TablesList calls duckDB.RunCommands and will always fail, so even when FlagSqlExpressions were enabled in future, any SQL expression would fail with 'error serializing sql: not implemented'. There's no test covering TablesList/QueryFramesInto behavior change, so broken functionality isn't caught in CI.

findings.title: No tests updated/added for disabled SQL execution path
findings.body: The PR disables the DuckDB-backed SQL engine by stubbing it out, but no tests were added or updated to verify that SQLCommand.Execute now fails gracefully, or that ReadQuery rejects QueryTypeSQL properly in all code paths (e.g., UnmarshalSQLCommand doesn't check the feature flag at all, so legacy/alerting code paths that call UnmarshalSQLCommand directly bypass the ReadQuery-level block and will reach the broken Execute path silently).

findings.title: UnmarshalSQLCommand does not check feature flag / enablement before constructing command
findings.body: UnmarshalSQLCommand (used for legacy raw-node parsing, e.g. in alerting) builds a SQLCommand without any check against enableSqlExpressions or the FlagSqlExpressions toggle, unlike ReadQuery which blocks QueryTypeSQL. This means code paths that use UnmarshalSQLCommand instead of ReadQuery could still attempt to construct and execute SQL commands, which only fail later via the stubbed db.go (and only because of that side effect), rather than being explicitly disabled. This is fragile: if db.go stub is removed/replaced in future without restoring the check here, the vulnerable code path reopens silently.
